correctness.rationale: For each ring, averaging the intensity at the four points, taking its first Fourier mode, and taking its real Nyquist mode account for exactly four real degrees of freedom. The first-mode radial matrix has determinant rs(s²−r²) and the normalized Nyquist angular determinant has absolute value |sin(2(ψ−φ))|. Under both conditions all off-diagonal Hermitian entries vanish in the kernel, and the two remaining radial constraints leave exactly the diagonal line generated by diag(r²s²,−(r²+s²),1). Its nonzero elements have rank three, excluding differences of two rank-one lifts even when one vector is zero. At equal radii the constant r and z collide; at sin(2(ψ−φ))=0, 1±i exp(−2iφ)z² collide. For seven or fewer measurements, a nonspanning family gives immediate failure; otherwise the at-least-two-dimensional Hermitian kernel contains a nonzero singular matrix by oddness of the determinant on a circle in any two-plane. It cannot be semidefinite and so is an indefinite rank-two difference of lifts. Finally the angular row Gram matrix has unit diagonal and cosine off-diagonal, proving the claimed singular values and optimum for that block only. This is an independent algebraic replay of frozen RESULT.md lines 31–69. The packaged checker was inspected, not executed.
